proposals.evidence: Ordered girl + child: DEDR364 explicitly gives Konda ayli daughter/girl and2149 koṛo female child, plural koṛok. These survey ayli koṛo/ayli koṛok responses retain both lexical constituents and the source woman gloss, including the plural form; the proposed analysis does not silently turn the prompt into girl.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3999 explicitly labels Konda pāta ‘cloth’ as borrowed from Telugu and gives Telugu pāta ‘old, decayed; an old cloth, a cloth’. The proposed immediate donor is that existing Telugu cloth attestation, not the unrelated pāṭa ‘song’; the survey pāṭa preserves a retroflex spelling difference requiring review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5153 gives Tamil/Malayalam āṇṭu year and Konda ēṇḍad year. Mannan āṇḍɨ is a comparative southern-lect extension; Konda yēṇḍa/yēṇḍaḍ are survey variants of the explicitly attested Konda noun, with initial glide and final segment preserved. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
